sections.What we use it for:
Every project under `tooling/` targets `net10.0`. The SDK compiles them, runs the three test layers, and packs the CLI as a dotnet tool.

`global.json` at the repository root pins the SDK at 10.0.402. Its `rollForward` is `disable`, so `dotnet` refuses to build with any other SDK, even a later patch installed beside it. [tol-setup-dotnet](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/134c546202285a1837fb2844058244b9ad9a91b1/examples/dog-fooding/tools/workflows/setup-dotnet.md) reads the file and installs that version in every job that builds, tests, packs or publishes with `dotnet`. A contributor installs the same version to build locally.

Dependabot raises each new 10.0 SDK as a pull request that moves the pin, and ignores a new major. The `versions` field states the pinned version, so that pull request moves it to match.
sections.Licence and obligations:
Microsoft licenses the product distribution under MIT on Linux and macOS. On Windows most files are MIT too, and Microsoft's [Windows licence information](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/license-information-windows.md) names the files that are not:

* The [.NET Library License](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/dotnet_library_license.htm) covers `coreclr.dll` and `Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native.*.dll`, among others.
* The [Windows SDK License](https://learn.microsoft.com/legal/windows-sdk/license) covers `D3DCompiler_47_cor3.dll`, which the WPF runtime uses.

The `round-trip` and `import-round-trip` jobs in `kac.yml` install the SDK on `windows-latest`, so `licence` includes both. Neither has an SPDX identifier, so each is a `LicenseRef-`. The Windows zip of SDK 10.0.402 contains every file the page names, and its root `LICENSE.txt` is the .NET Library License.

The SDK also puts a `ThirdPartyNotices.txt` of 56 notices beside its `LICENSE.txt`, and the file is the same on Windows and macOS. Every notice is permissive or a public-domain dedication, and `licence` lists each one SPDX has an identifier for. The rest are bare permission grants SPDX does not list: ISO 8879, RFC 3492, RFC 4122, and code its author released with no named licence. Nothing in the file is copyleft.

Nothing follows for a package this repository publishes. The .NET Library License allows installing and using the software to design, develop and test programs, which is what CI does with it. CI redistributes no part of the SDK.
sections.Where it is used:
* [svc-corpus-feed](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/134c546202285a1837fb2844058244b9ad9a91b1/examples/dog-fooding/services/corpus-feed.md) is packed by `kac`, which runs on it.
* [svc-kac](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/134c546202285a1837fb2844058244b9ad9a91b1/examples/dog-fooding/services/kac.md) is built, tested and packed with it.
* [svc-marketplace](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/134c546202285a1837fb2844058244b9ad9a91b1/examples/dog-fooding/services/marketplace.md) is bundled by `kac`, which runs on it.

The docs site is built by another toolchain, so it does not use the SDK.
